title: Candidate Manager / Resourcer
description:
Candidate Manager

Leeds City Centre Full-Time Permanent

Are you a people person with excellent communication skills and a proactive approach to work? Looking to build a long-term career with a growing, award-winning recruitment business?

Prospero Teaching is one of the UK's leading education recruitment agencies, and due to continued growth, we're looking for a Candidate Manager to join our successful Children's Educational Services (CES) team in Leeds.

In this role, you'll be responsible for sourcing, screening and supporting candidates, helping to connect talented education professionals with opportunities that make a real difference to young people's lives.

Key Responsibilities:
- Source and attract candidates through job boards, LinkedIn and referrals
- Conduct candidate screening calls and Teams interviews
- Manage candidate registrations and onboarding
- Build strong relationships with candidates throughout the recruitment process
- Create candidate profiles and support consultants with live vacancies
- Work closely with Compliance Officers to ensure candidate files are complete
- Deliver an exceptional candidate experience

What We're Looking For:
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills
- Highly organised with strong attention to detail
- Positive, motivated and proactive attitude
- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
- Recruitment, sales, customer service or administration experience is advantageous but not essential

Why Join Prospero?
- Industry-leading training and development
- Clear progression opportunities
- Supportive and collaborative team culture
- Modern Leeds city centre office
- Opportunity to build a successful career within recruitment

If you're ambitious, driven and enjoy working with people, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today!

title: Compliance Administrator- Leading Recruitment Company
description:
Join Prospero Teaching - Where Passion Meets Purpose in Education!

For over 20 years, Prospero Teaching has been a trusted leader in connecting teaching and support staff with schools, academies, and nurseries across the UK and internationally. We proudly offer our services to a broad range of educational settings, including EYFS, Primary, Secondary, Further Education, SEN, and PRUs.

About the Role

As a Compliance Administrator, you will be a key member of our compliance team, responsible for ensuring candidates meet the necessary regulatory and internal requirements to work within the education sector. You will play a vital role in maintaining compliance with industry standards and fostering a smooth recruitment process for candidates.

Key Responsibilities
- Collaborate with the compliance team to ensure candidates meet all compliance standards for the education sector.
- Follow established operational processes and procedures to ensure adherence to regulations and industry standards.
- Guide and support candidates throughout the recruitment process.
- Conduct compliance checks, including but not limited to right-to-work, DBS, reference, and employment history verifications.
- Maintain and update accurate candidate records.
- Organise and verify candidate documentation.
- Respond to both internal and external inquiries efficiently and professionally.

About You

We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented individual with:
- A good general education (minimum GCSEs in Maths and English, grades A-C, or equivalent).
- Strong relationship-building skills.
- The ability to work effectively under deadlines.
- Excellent administrative and organizational abilities, with a talent for prioritizing tasks.
- Strong communication and customer service skills.
- An understanding of confidentiality and data protection.
- A proactive problem-solving mindset.
- A commitment to safeguarding practices.

Benefits
- Competitive salary with a commission structure.
- Ongoing training and opportunities for professional development.
- Clear career advancement prospects within the company.
- A dynamic and collaborative work environment.
- Private healthcare.
- Quarterly performance-based incentives.

Join us and be part of a team that's helping drive one of the UK's fastest-growing recruitment firms forward.

title: HR Coordinator
description:
HR Coordinator
East Leeds
32,000- 35,000
Your new role
We are working with a business in Leeds who are looking to appoint an HR Coordinator to support the day-to-day delivery of HR operations across a growing business. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced HR Administrator looking to step into a broader HR role or an established HR Coordinator seeking their next challenge.
Working closely with the HR Manager and wider leadership team, you will play a key role in ensuring a positive employee experience by providing efficient HR support throughout the employee life cycle.What you'll need to succeed
- Coordinate onboarding and induction processes for new starters.
- Prepare contracts, offer letters and employment documentation.
- Maintain accurate employee records and HR databases.
- Support recruitment activities, including interview scheduling and candidate communication.
- Process employee changes, including promotions, salary reviews and contractual amendments.
- Monitor probation periods and support performance review processes.
- Manage absence records, holiday requests and HR reporting.
- Assist with payroll preparation and provide payroll information to external providers.
- Act as the first point of contact for employee HR queries.
- Previous experience in an HR Administrator, HR Assistant or HR Coordinator role.
- Strong understanding of HR processes and employment life cycle activities.
- Excellent organisational skills with strong attention to detail.
- Confident communicator with the ability to build relationships at all levels.
- Able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

What you need to do now
If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.
If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

title: Recruitment Resourcer
description:
Recruitment Resourcer
Aqumen Recruitment

Salary: £26,000 per annum
Location: Carrwood Park, Selby Road, Leeds, LS15 4 LG
Contract: Full-time, permanent
Hours: Monday to Friday, 9.00am 5.30pm

Aqumen Recruitment is looking for an organised, enthusiastic Recruitment Resourcer to support our temporary, permanent and event recruitment teams.

Reporting to the Operations Director, you ll help with day-to-day recruitment activity, maintain accurate candidate records and ensure candidates are interviewed and fully briefed on job opportunities.

Your main duties will include:
- Supporting recruitment across our temporary, permanent and event recruitment teams.
- Accurately updating our CRM, ensuring candidate information and recruitment activity are recorded correctly.
- Interviewing candidates to understand their skills, experience, availability and suitability for roles.
- Briefing candidates on job roles, including duties, working hours, location and expectations.
- Maintaining clear, professional communication with candidates throughout the recruitment process.
- Following company procedures for candidate registration, right-to-work checks, confidentiality and data protection.

We re looking for someone who:
- Communicates clearly and confidently with candidates and colleagues.
- Is organised, pays close attention to detail and maintains accurate records.
- Is comfortable using computer systems and learning new platforms.
- Can manage competing priorities and work across different recruitment teams.
- Is keen to learn and handles confidential information professionally.
- Preferably have a Driving License and a car.

In return, we offer:
- 25 days annual leave plus statutory holidays.
- Training and development, including access to the Savage Recruitment Academy, coaching from experienced colleagues and training from external providers.
- Practical training in our CRM, candidate registration, right-to-work processes, GDPR and other relevant platforms.
- A NEST workplace pension.
- A company laptop and mobile phone for work use.
- An Employee Assistance Programme.
- Reimbursement for hearing and eye tests against valid receipts.
- Reimbursement of eligible business expenses and mileage in line with company policy.

Our current informal working arrangement allows homeworking on Wednesdays and Fridays, subject to business needs and attendance at the office when required.

Our office at Carrwood Park is set within 100 acres of Yorkshire countryside. Employees can enjoy events throughout the year, including summer picnics by the lake, pizza parties and a bonfire and fireworks display that family members can attend free of charge.

If you enjoy working with people, keeping things organised and helping candidates prepare for their next role, we d like to hear from you.

To apply: Send your CV

Appointment is subject to verification of your right to work in the UK.

title: Temporary HR Administrator - DSAR Project
description:
Temporary HR Administrator - DSAR Project

We're recruiting for an exciting temporary opportunity with a corporate financial services company based in Leeds city centre.

Location: Leeds city centre
Start date: Immediate
Duration: Approximately 4-8 weeks
Pay rate: 17.90 per hour plus holiday pay
Hours: Monday to Friday, 37.5 hours per week

The Opportunity

We're looking for a detail-oriented HR Administrator to support a time-sensitive Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) project. This role would suit someone with experience in HR administration, auditing, compliance or confidential document review who is confident handling sensitive information and identifying potential risks.
You'll review information retrieved through Mimecast, manually checking emails, folders and documents to identify relevant information and prepare records for redaction and further review.

Key Responsibilities
- Review emails, folders and documents retrieved through Mimecast in response to DSARs.
- Manually examine records to identify information relevant to each request.
- Upload or transfer documents into the designated review system.
- Identify and redact confidential or sensitive information in line with project guidelines.
- Review email correspondence, highlighting information requiring redaction or further investigation.
- Flag potential risks and document the rationale for each decision.
- Apply an understanding of HR processes to identify sensitive employee information and potential risks.
- Maintain accurate records, ensuring all reviews are completed consistently and confidentially.

About You
- Previous experience in HR administration, auditing, compliance, records management or document review.
- An understanding of HR processes and confidential employee information.
- Excellent attention to detail, with the ability to review large volumes of information accurately.
- Confidence identifying sensitive data, potential risks and information requiring escalation.
- Strong written communication skills, particularly when documenting findings and explaining decisions.
- A professional and discreet approach to handling highly confidential information.

Desirable Experience
- Previous experience completing Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs).
- Knowledge of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.
- Experience using redaction or eDiscovery tools.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong HR administration or auditing experience who enjoys detailed, process-driven work and can quickly identify sensitive information and potential risks.
